readings: Join invoices to orders to customers, dropping any that don't link up. For each Customers.gender value, count the DISTINCT orders that have at least one invoice, so an order with several invoices counts once. Each gender's share is its count divided by the sum of these counts over all genders. The average share is the mean of the shares across the genders present, which is 1 divided by the number of genders. List only the genders whose share is strictly above that average. For each, give the gender, the count, the share, and the share minus the average share (an absolute difference). Don't round anything.

Join invoices to orders to customers, dropping any that don't link up. For each Customers.gender value, count the invoice rows (invoice_number), so an order with several invoices counts once per invoice. Each gender's share is its count divided by the sum of these counts over all genders. The average share is the mean of the shares across the genders present, which is 1 divided by the number of genders. List only the genders whose share is strictly above that average. For each, give the gender, the count, the share, and the share minus the average share (an absolute difference). Don't round anything.
queries:
WITH g AS (
  SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS cnt
  FROM Invoices i
  JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.gender
),
t AS (
  SELECT gender, cnt,
         CAST(cnt AS REAL) / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share,
         1.0 / COUNT(*) OVER () AS avg_share
  FROM g
)
SELECT gender, cnt AS count, share, ABS(share - avg_share) AS diff_from_avg
FROM t
WHERE share > avg_share;
WITH g AS (
  SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(i.invoice_number) AS cnt
  FROM Invoices i
  JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.gender
),
t AS (
  SELECT gender, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM g) AS share,
         1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM g) AS avg_share
  FROM g
)
SELECT gender, cnt AS count, share, ABS(share - avg_share) AS diff_from_average
FROM t
WHERE share > avg_share;
